$comment: Repo Governor governing its own repository. Canonical format is JSON (ADR-015). This file is the sole artifact that binds providers to roles (ADR-004); a provider absent here has no governance role, however reachable it is (INV-013).

condition.$comment: L1: one package, small dependency surface, one maintainer. Not L0 — architecture history exists. No floor indicator present: no public API, no release branches, no generated consumers.

roadmap_authority.$comment: GitHub issues are this repository's roadmap. The file provider was bound here until 2026-08-17 and became a second roadmap of record -- section 54's oldest failure condition, reproduced inside the tool built to prevent it (ADR-022, issue 19). The file fixture now lives in conformance/fixtures/ and is never bound.

admission.$comment: ADR-018: declared, never assumed. Milestone membership is admission here. Consequence accepted: an issue with no milestone reads NOT_ADMITTED, which is the correct reading for deferrals like 6 and 14.

acceptance_criteria.$comment: Repo-local acceptance artifacts (ADR-017), keyed by GitHub issue number now that GitHub is the roadmap authority. Synthetic criteria used by conformance live in conformance/fixtures/acceptance/ and are reached by env override, never bound here.

decision_history.$comment: ADR-019. Dolt supplies the evidence chain natively (dolt_log, dolt_history_decisions), so ADR-009's hand-specified hash chaining is superseded rather than reimplemented.

Second backend. GitHub already records decisions in stateReason and nothing was reading them. Bound alongside Dolt because decision_history is multi-valued (ADR-013); disagreement is CONFLICT, not precedence. Repository identity is declared here because the adapter no longer defaults it (ADR-028, issue 26).

Third backend, bound for PORTABILITY. The Dolt store is gitignored on the reasoning that Dolt has its own remotes; no remote was ever configured, so it was distributed by nothing and a decommissioned host took the chain with it. This adapter writes .repo-governor/decisions/decisions.jsonl -- text, tracked, and it supplies reversal_condition and revision_history, the two capabilities decision-history-github cannot. ADR-019 rule 2 anticipated exactly this pairing: a second backend bound alongside is how portability gets tested rather than asserted. Its chain is hand-rolled sha256 links and it says so in `properties`, per ADR-019 rule 3.

providers.$comment: Six roles bound. `execution` and `change_signals` are deliberately UNBOUND: this repository has no execution tracker and no dependency-signal source, and the file providers previously bound to them read synthetic fixtures under .repo-governor/. Binding a role to a fixture makes the fixture the repository's state -- which is how the roadmap became a shadow roadmap (ADR-022). An unbound role yields a typed disposition, which is the honest answer; a fixture-backed one yields a confident wrong answer.

permissions.$comment: Deny by default (ADR-005). Read-only throughout: Repo Governor rules, it does not act.

decision_history.$comment: The only write granted anywhere in this manifest. ADR-005 rule 4 treats write as exceptional and read as presumed; this is the exception, because the engine recording its own decisions is what makes INV-005 enforceable. Every other role stays read-only.
